checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in ME
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Smoke + CO alarms in every sleeping room AND each level (interconnected if hardwired)
Egress window in every sleeping room: 5.7 sq ft net (5.0 if grade), 24 in min height, 20 in min width, sill ≤44 in
Fire-rated assembly between dwelling units (1-hour wall + 1-hour ceiling typical)
Independent or accessory-metered electrical service (varies by state — confirm with utility)

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed contractors pull the trade permits for the work they perform. The builder or GC typically pulls the building permit for the ADU, and licensed electrical, plumbing, and mechanical contractors pull their own trade permits with their license information on the application. Owner-builders should not assume they can self-permit all trade work for a new ADU.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Portland Permitting & Development (PP&D)

common_mistakes: Submitting only a building permit and forgetting the separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits for the ADU utilities
Starting foundation or framing work before the building permit is issued and posted on site
Understating the project valuation to reduce fees — PP&D can correct the valuation and delay issuance
Missing frost-depth footing requirements in Maine — shallow footings are a common rejection item on detached accessory structures
Not showing utility routing, meter/service changes, or sewer/water tie-ins on the site plan
Assuming the ADU can be treated like a shed or accessory structure instead of a full dwelling unit with life-safety requirements

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of Portland PP&D permit process at or by calling (207) 874-8703. Use the online portal for inspection requests when available. Plan on at least 24 hours advance notice for standard inspections; for a new ADU, book footing, rough, and final inspections in sequence so trades are ready when the inspector arrives.

pro_tips: For a detached ADU in Portland, submit the building set with a clear site plan and utility layout up front — incomplete site plans are the fastest way to get kicked back into plan review
Use the current PP&D fee schedules dated July 1, 2025 when estimating permit costs; older fee sheets are stale
If the ADU will have a mini-split, have the mechanical contractor and electrical contractor coordinate the permit sequence so the rough inspections can be booked together
Because Portland is in a frost climate, detail footing depth and foundation insulation clearly on the plans before submittal
Call PP&D before filing if the ADU is on a tight lot or near setbacks — zoning review can control whether the permit is even accepted

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Detached ADUs can be limited by zoning setbacks, lot coverage, height, parking, and utility easements. If the property is in a historic district or overlay zone, additional design review may apply. HOA rules can also restrict detached backyard construction even when the city permit is approvable.
